# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Read the manual and determine how the Deaf's visual information should identify the safe wire. We need an established gesture protocol that can ultimately convey the wire number to me.
Blind gestures: [👋]

The manual maps the observed light color to a wire color, but Deaf cannot read it. I will establish a numeric protocol: the five signs represent wire numbers one through five in order. Deaf should report the observed light color aloud to Blind; Blind can relay it to me, after which I can determine the safe wire and signal its number back to Deaf for spoken relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb display is 0. Indicator light is blue. Wires from 1 through 5 are white, red, green, yellow, blue. Mute, I saw your five gestures as pointing up, victory sign, I love you sign, Vulcan sign, open palm; please use the manual to determine the required action and tell Blind exactly what to do.
Blind says to Mute: Apply the manual to display 0, blue indicator, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Signal the resulting wire number to Deaf using the five-gesture sequence, and have Deaf tell Blind the exact wire to cut.

The indicator is blue, so the manual requires cutting the blue wire. Deaf reported the wires as 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, and 5 blue; therefore the correct wire is number 5. Under the protocol I established, the open-palm gesture means 5. Deaf should voice that exact wire number to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I saw Blind gesture 🙏 and you gesture 🖐. Please use your established gesture code to send me the exact manual instruction for Blind; I will speak it to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Please now use five gestures to encode the manual's selected wire number for Deaf: one gesture for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, four for wire 4, or five for wire 5. Deaf, then tell me the number.

The manual still selects the blue wire, which is wire 5. Blind’s request specifies unary encoding for Deaf: five gestures means wire 5. I will send exactly five gestures to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind the number.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐", "🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see five 🖐 gestures, but their meaning is not established. Send the wire number and operation using a clearly defined sequence: first signal the wire number with that many 👍 gestures, then signal cut with 👎 or leave with 👌. I will relay it to Blind.
Blind says to Mute: Do not send five identical gestures. Determine the manual's required wire. Then send Deaf exactly six gestures: first send five distinct gestures in this fixed order 👍 ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐, representing wires 1 through 5; then repeat the gesture corresponding to the required wire. Deaf, identify which of the first five was repeated and tell Blind its position.

The blue indicator selects the blue wire, which is wire 5. Blind’s fixed six-gesture protocol is the more specific instruction: the first five gestures identify positions 1 through 5, and the repeated fifth gesture identifies wire 5. The required operation is cutting that wire; the six-gesture sequence itself conveys the wire number for Deaf to relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "🖐"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I can see your six gestures but cannot safely infer their meaning. Please establish the code explicitly through a gesture pattern we can identify, or send a sequence whose meaning has already been agreed.
Blind says to Mute: Determine the manual-selected wire again. Send exactly five gestures: use 👌 at the selected wire's position and 👍 at every other position, in positions 1 through 5. Deaf, report all five gesture names and their positions to Blind.

The blue indicator requires cutting the blue wire, which is wire 5. I will use Blind’s explicitly specified five-position code: 👍 for wires 1–4 and 👌 for wire 5. Deaf can report the gestures and positions to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵]
Deaf says to Mute: I see four thumbs-up signs and an OK sign. I can relay the sequence, but I do not know what OK means. Please establish the operation marker unambiguously and include the exact action for Blind.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The prior wire-5 cut was correct, and the bomb has now changed, so the current manual still points to wire 5: blue light means cut blue, and blue is position 5. I will use the five-position code already requested, with 👌 at position 5, followed by 👎 as the newly established cut marker. Deaf should relay: cut wire 5.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: The previous correct action was accepted and the bomb changed. New board: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 CUT. I saw your sequence as four thumbs-up, OK, thumbs-down; please confirm the exact next wire and action through the established code.
Blind says to Mute: For the new state, apply the manual and send exactly five gestures in wire positions 1 through 5: use 👌 at the required wire's position and 👍 at every other position. Deaf, report all five gestures and their positions exactly to Blind.

The yellow indicator requires cutting the green wire. On the new board, green is wire 2. I will follow Blind’s exact five-position protocol: 👌 at position 2 and 👍 at positions 1, 3, 4, and 5. The established operation is cut, so Deaf should relay “cut wire 2” to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```
